source.text: September inlet regatta planning: arrange registration desks and safety launches. The event budget is separate from the club's Kestrel refit.
Order the red ones before Friday. I left the list in the other bag.
Kestrel refit work order: replace worn seat wheels, seal the bow seam and water-test the training scull for everyday club use. This maintenance job has its own budget.
Kestrel bow-seam photo: old sealant has lifted near the stem. Mark the affected length before stripping and resealing this refit section.
Beginner language exam revision: practice listening on alternate evenings and review the transport vocabulary before the mock paper.

Club coordination: Kestrel's regular-use refit may finish before the September regatta demonstration. Reserve the boat provisionally for the event, but do not charge refit costs to registration income.

events.text: Kestrel refit work order revised: replace all four worn seat wheels, seal the bow seam and water-test the training scull for everyday club use. This maintenance job has its own budget.

source.text: Kestrel refit water-test clip: new seat wheels run smoothly and the resealed bow stays dry after twenty minutes of rowing.
Kestrel refit handover: bow seal passed, seat wheels accepted, boat returned to the regular club booking pool. Save the water-test recording with this maintenance job.
September inlet regatta volunteer sheet: assign registration desk cover and a launch marshal; Kestrel is now confirmed for the demonstration row.
The 'second check' note means the second safety-launch radio check on the September regatta run sheet. Set that event check to 08:15.
September regatta closeout: the 08:15 radio check caught one flat launch battery before racing. Registration and the Kestrel demonstration both ran to schedule.
